chunks: 5. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashm narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a man from the Kharijites entered and asked him: 'O Abu Ja'far, whom do you worship?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Allah.' He asked: 'Have you seen Him?' He (peace be upon him) answered: 'Eyes do not see Him through direct vision, but hearts see Him through the realities of faith. He is not known by analogy, nor perceived by the senses, nor compared to people. He is described by signs, known by indications, does not act unjustly in His judgment. That is Allah; there is no god but Him.' The man left while saying: 'Allah knows best where to place His Message.'

key_terms.الْخَوَارِج: Kharijites, a early Islamic sect known for their theological views
key_terms.لَا يَجُورُ فِي حُكْمِهِ: Does not act unjustly in His judgment

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars define the vision of God according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the Shia doctrine of *Basar* (vision), distinguishing between physical sight (*ru'yat al-ayn*) which cannot grasp God's essence, and spiritual insight (*ru'yat al-qalb*) achieved through faith. It underscores that God is transcendent and unlike creation (*laysa ka-mithlihi shay*), known only through His signs and attributes, a concept central to resolving debates with groups like the Khawarij. The narrative highlights the intellectual depth of the Imams in articulating divine transcendence using concise, Quranic terminology.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. My Father (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashimsaid on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ma`bad, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, on the authority of his father that

I was in the presence of Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) when a Kharijite entered his presence and asked him: “O Abu Ja`far, who do you serve?” He (AS) replied: “Allah.” He questioned: “Have you seen Him?” He (AS) answered: Eyes cannot see him through vision, but hearts can see Him through certainty of faith. He is neither recognized with analogy, nor perceived with the senses, and cannot be compared to people. He is attributed through signs and recognized through indications. There is no oppression in His Judgement. Such is Allah; there is no god but Him. He said: “Then the man left while saying that `Allah knows best where to place His Message.”
